questions.question: In a roughly normal distribution, about what share of values lie within 2 standard deviations of the mean?
questions.explanation: The empirical rule: about 68% within 1 SD, 95% within 2 SD, 99.7% within 3 SD.

questions.question: Increasing the standard deviation of a normal distribution makes the curve...
questions.explanation: σ controls the spread. A larger σ spreads the same total area (1) over a wider range, so the peak is lower and the curve flatter. The mean controls the position.

questions.question: IQ ~ N(100, 15). Which range holds about 95% of people?
Exam scores ~ N(72, 11). A student scores 90. What is z, and roughly what share scores higher?
questions.explanation: z = (90 − 72) ÷ 11 ≈ 1.64. The table gives P(Z < 1.64) ≈ 0.9495, so about 1 − 0.9495 ≈ 5% scored higher.

questions.question: The z-table gives P(Z < 1) = 0.8413 and P(Z < −1) = 0.1587. What is P(−1 < Z < 1)?
questions.explanation: Between = upper area − lower area = 0.8413 − 0.1587 = 0.6827, the familiar 68%.

questions.question: Heights ~ N(69.1, 2.9) inches. The 90th percentile has z ≈ 1.28. What is that height?
questions.explanation: x = μ + zσ = 69.1 + 1.28 × 2.9 ≈ 72.8 inches. Going from a percentile back to a value uses z = (x − μ)/σ rearranged.
